subject: Quantline demo follow-up — recommended model shortlist and operational asks
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@quantline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@quantline.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick post-demo notes + questions

Ben — thanks again for the walkthrough today. High level we liked Redwood’s latency profile and the idea of prefix caching for our templated responses. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

1) Can you consolidate which models we should evaluate first given our requirements (real-time chat, 99th-pct latency target ~120ms, priority on answer accuracy for finance domain)?
2) Any benchmark artifacts or prompt-set examples we can run locally to validate?
3) What are the expected per-token costs for the suggested shortlist (ballpark)?

We’d like a short prioritized list and a plan to run a 2-week pilot if the numbers check out.

Best,
Samir Gupta
Head of ML, Quantline

--
Attachment: demo-deck.pdf (presentation stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@quantline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes + questions

Samir — great to be syncing. Below is a concise recommended shortlist and rationale — focused on balancing your accuracy bar (finance QA), 99th latency target, and cost sensitivity for a pilot. I’ve attached a small benchmark CSV and a starter prompt set you can run locally.

Shortlist (priority order):
- redwood-edu-13b-q4 (Candidate A) — Best accuracy on finance evaluation set; runs well with 16-bit quantization; estimated p95/p99 latency fits your 120ms goal on T4-like hardware with our continuous batching off for real-time TN. Ballpark cost: ~$0.045/token for generation workload in pilot config.
- open-econ-34b-qa-lite (Candidate B) — Strong factuality for numeric reasoning, slightly higher latency but higher throughput if batched; good fallback option when accuracy-critical prompts run. Ballpark cost: ~$0.09/token.
- compact-synth-7b (Candidate C) — Lightweight, low-latency (<40ms p95) for assistant glue code and prompt scaffolding; useful to move non-critical generation off the primary model to save cost. Ballpark cost: ~$0.012/token.

Rationale highlights:
- We recommend A for the 2-week pilot as the primary model; B as an accuracy fallback for heavy numeric tasks; C for cheap pre/post-processing. That mix keeps your unit economics reasonable while protecting quality.
- We’ll enable prefix/KV caching for repeated templates and conservative batching (max batch size 4, batch wait 5ms) to meet your 99th percentile latency SLO.

Included artifacts (attached): 
- quantline_model_benchmarks.csv — p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput across representative prompt lengths (5–250 tokens)
- prompt_set_v1.txt — 40 prompt seeds including financial Q/A, balance reconciliation, and numeric roll-ups to surface regressions
- mutual_action_plan_QTL4932.pdf — proposed pilot timeline and success metrics (SLA, accuracy thresholds, cost guardrails)

Next steps (proposed):
1) You run the prompt_set_v1 locally against the attached CSV inputs to sanity-check quality (we included expected outputs for reference).
2) Redwood will provision a small dedicated test pool for your pilot (estimate 2–3 days) once we sign the pilot MPA.
3) Quick sync this week to finalize metrics and procurement path.

Cc’ing Marissa to coordinate commercial path and Monica for ops requirements.

Thanks — happy to refine.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0149

--
Attachments: quantline_model_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, mutual_action_plan_QTL4932.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@quantline.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes + questions

Samir — quick note from commercial: for a pilot we typically set a 30–45 day MPA (pilot terms) with a capped commit (to limit your exposure). I’ve pulled together a draft MPA and a short procurement checklist: 

- Draft pilot MPA (terms: pilot-only SLA / data handling / termination window)
- PO or credit-card billing allowed for pilot (depending on procurement policy)
- If you prefer an SOW + invoice path we can do that but it adds approval time (2–3 weeks)

If you can share who on your procurement team we should loop in (name + contact), we’ll fast-track a draft and get it ready for signature.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

--
(Attachment referenced: pilot_MPA_draft.docx — not included in thread attachments list until you confirm procurement route)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@quantline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes + questions

Operational note on latency/cost tradeoffs — hi team, quick hit: 

- The p99 constraints are achievable with Candidate A if we: (a) reserve a small Dedicated pool (2 x A100 or equivalent) for baseline, (b) use KV caching for any repeated templates, and (c) set conservative autoscale burst thresholds. That keeps tail latency stable while letting you handle spikes.
- For monitoring: we’ll surface token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per-route in the console and put regression alerts on the prompt_set_v1 seeds.
- Cost-control levers during pilot: route non-critical prompts to Candidate C and enable per-route rate caps. Expect an initial uplift in infra cost during validation (~10–20%) that should normalize once caching/batching is tuned.

I attached a quick ops checklist for the pilot and a sample observability dashboard link (dashboard will be provisioned upon pool creation).

Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

--
Attachment: pilot_ops_checklist.md (stub)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@quantline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes + questions

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick clarifications before we run the seeds: 

- For Candidate A, can you confirm the p99 numbers in the CSV were recorded with no batching? If not, what is the difference between batching off vs batch size 4 (we’ll emulate real-time traffic with minimal batching).
- On cost: are the ballpark numbers inclusive of prefix/KV cache savings or raw per-token compute only?

Procurement: I’ll loop in our procurement lead, Priya Shah, and she’s cc’d. She prefers an MPA route with a PO. Priya — can you share your PO process cadence?

If we can confirm the two items above by EOD Wednesday we’ll kick off running the prompt set and then request the pilot MPA.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Samir
